title: Mapping the Global Future: Report of the National Intelligence Council's 2020 Project
notes: Third edition, known as Global Trends 2020. Published December 2004 (date as cited in Global Trends 2025, footnote 3: 'National Intelligence Council, December 2004'); no report number found in the web text. Read from the Wayback copies (2006) of the dni.gov HTML edition (executive summary, methodology, introduction, four sections, policy implications); the PDF edition was not located in the Wayback index. Scope: the 2020 Global Landscape table and Executive Summary (projections the NIC states in its own voice) and the four fictional scenarios as summarized under 'Possible Futures'. Body sections were downloaded but not mined. Figures attributed to others (US Census Bureau population projections for China and India) are excluded. Horizon 2020 has passed.

entries.label: US remains single most powerful actor
entries.quote: US will remain single most powerful actor economically, technologically, militarily.
entries.subject: US global role

entries.label: China's GNP exceeds every Western economy except the US
entries.quote: Most forecasts indicate that by 2020 China’s gross national product (GNP) will exceed that of individual Western economic powers except for the United States.
entries.subject: China economy
entries.metric: China GNP rank among major economies
entries.note: Executive Summary, New Global Players. Framed as 'most forecasts indicate'; forecasters not named. Measure (market rates or PPP) not stated.

entries.label: India's GNP overtaking European economies
entries.quote: India’s GNP will have overtaken or be on the threshold of overtaking European economies.
entries.subject: India
entries.note: Executive Summary. Which European economies is not stated.

entries.label: Brazil and Indonesia approach European economies
entries.quote: The economies of other developing countries, such as Brazil, could surpass all but the largest European countries by 2020; Indonesia’s economy could also approach the economies of individual European countries by 2020.
entries.subject: emerging economies

entries.label: North Korea crisis comes to a head within 15 years
entries.quote: the crisis over North Korea is likely to come to a head sometime over the next 15 years.
entries.subject: North Korea

entries.label: World economy 80 percent larger than in 2000
entries.quote: by 2020, it is projected to be about 80 percent larger than it was in 2000, and average per capita income will be roughly 50 percent higher.
entries.subject: global economic growth
entries.metric: world economy size vs 2000; average per capita income vs 2000
entries.note: Executive Summary, Impact of Globalization. 'it' is the world economy. Conditional on no catastrophic reversal of globalization.

entries.label: Energy consumption up about 50 percent in two decades
entries.quote: Total energy consumed probably will rise by about 50 percent in the next two decades compared to a 34 percent expansion from 1980-2000, with a greater share provided by petroleum.
entries.subject: energy demand
entries.metric: growth in total world energy consumption
entries.note: Executive Summary. Comparison with 1980-2000 implies 2000-2020; read as 2020. Also states petroleum's share rises.

entries.label: Political Islam has significant global impact to 2020
entries.quote: political Islam will have a significant global impact leading to 2020, rallying disparate ethnic and national groups and perhaps even creating an authority that transcends national boundaries.
entries.subject: political Islam
entries.note: Executive Summary, New Challenges to Governance.

entries.label: Third wave of democratization may be partly reversed
entries.quote: The so-called “third wave” of democratization may be partially reversed by 2020—particularly among the states of the former Soviet Union and in Southeast Asia, some of which never really embraced democracy.
entries.subject: democracy

entries.label: Great power total war less likely than at any time in the past century
entries.quote: The likelihood of great power conflict escalating into total war in the next 15 years is lower than at any time in the past century
entries.subject: great power conflict
entries.note: Executive Summary, Pervasive Insecurity. Also in the landscape table: 'Great power conflict escalating into total war unlikely.'

entries.label: Nuclear states improve survivability and delivery systems
entries.quote: Current nuclear weapons states will continue to improve the survivability of their deterrent forces and almost certainly will improve the reliability, accuracy, and lethality of their delivery systems as well as develop capabilities to penetrate missile defenses.
entries.subject: nuclear weapons

entries.label: al-Qa'ida superseded by similar groups by 2020
entries.quote: We expect that by 2020 al-Qa’ida will be superceded by similarly inspired Islamic extremist groups, and there is a substantial risk that broad Islamic movements akin to al-Qa’ida will merge with local separatist movements.
entries.subject: terrorism
entries.note: Executive Summary, Transmuting International Terrorism. 'superceded' is as printed.

entries.label: Terrorist attacks mainly with conventional weapons
entries.quote: Terrorist attacks will continue to primarily employ conventional weapons, incorporating new twists and constantly adapting to counterterrorist efforts.
entries.subject: terrorism

entries.label: Davos World
entries.quote: Davos World provides an illustration of how robust economic growth, led by China and India, over the next 15 years could reshape the globalization process—giving it a more non-Western face and transforming the political playing field as well.
entries.subject: globalization
entries.note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 1.

entries.label: Pax Americana
entries.quote: Pax Americana takes a look at how US predominance may survive the radical changes to the global political landscape and serve to fashion a new and inclusive global order.
entries.subject: US global role
entries.note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 2.

entries.label: A New Caliphate
entries.quote: A New Caliphate provides an example of how a global movement fueled by radical religious identity politics could constitute a challenge to Western norms and values as the foundation of the global system.
entries.subject: political Islam
entries.note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 3.

entries.label: Cycle of Fear
entries.quote: Cycle of Fear provides an example of how concerns about proliferation might increase to the point that large-scale intrusive security measures are taken to prevent outbreaks of deadly attacks, possibly introducing an Orwellian world.
entries.subject: weapons of mass destruction
entries.note: Executive Summary, Possible Futures. Full narrative in section 4.

entries.label: EU, not NATO, becomes Europe's primary institution
entries.quote: The EU, rather than NATO, will increasingly become the primary institution for Europe
entries.subject: Europe
entries.note: Executive Summary, Policy Implications ('Some trends we probably can bank on').

entries.label: No country rivals US military power by 2020
entries.quote: While no single country looks within striking distance of rivaling US military power by 2020, more countries will be in a position to make the United States pay a heavy price for any military action they oppose.
entries.subject: US global role
